If asked questions about the Online Doctor of Education in Agricultural Education, answer with

The joint Ed.D. program (Doc@Distance) previously provided by Texas Tech University and Texas A&M University will not admit a cohort in 2019. This is a result of recent graduate program reviews at both universities and reflection on the future of the program.

If you are interested in pursuing a doctoral graduate degree via distance, you can still do so at Texas Tech University with the Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program.

The Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program builds on previous undergraduate and graduate courses along with their life experiences (including three years of related work experiences). It is designed to develop independent and critical thinking. Emphasis is placed on selecting courses and experiences that lead to a thorough and comprehensive knowledge of agricultural education and/or agricultural communications, a supporting field, and methods of research and statistics.

Step 1: This degree program requires a minimum of 72 semester hours of graduate coursework beyond the baccalaureate degree along with the development of a dissertation.

Step 2: At or near the end of coursework, the student will take a qualifying written examination consisting of eight hours for Agricultural Education, four hours for Research, Evaluation, and Statistics; and four hours for the Supporting Field.

Step 3: No more than one week after the written examination, the student will take an oral qualifying examination. Both of these examinations will be administered by the student's advisory committee (consisting of at least three members of the graduate faculty).

Step 4: After completion of the dissertation, the student will present and defend a dissertation.

Please note that this program is offered by main campus and is 100% Online - Asynchronous

Online+ is available to students after high school graduation who are attending college for the first time. Online+ is available to those with a high school diploma or GED. If the program you want to study is available online, you are not required to study on-campus and can complete your degree 100% online if relocating to the main campus is not an option.

Would Online+ be better for me since I work full time and I cannot attend class in person? Can I take all my classes online from the beginning of college?

The Texas Tech Online+ program is designed specifically for working professionals, providing the flexibility to complete your coursework fully online. This makes it an excellent choice for individuals who work full-time and cannot attend classes in person. You can take all your classes online from the beginning of your studies, as the program offers various online degree options that can accommodate your schedule. If you're interested in learning more or getting started with the Online+ program, please visit http://GoOnline.ttu.edu (opens in new tab) or contact them directly at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

Can I transfer credits into Texas Tech Online?

Yes! Texas Tech University accepts transfer credits, which are evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Contact an Enrollment Service Specialist (opens in new tab) to see how your prior coursework applies.

Link for "Enrollment Service Specialist (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/advocates/

How do I defer my start term?

Step 1: Discuss which term you are wanting to start in with your Online Student Advocate. Registration may be open already for your preferred term.

Step 2: Complete the Registrar Withdrawal process for the term you wish to drop to zero hours if you are enrolled in classes.

Step 3: Contact Admissions to let them know you have decided to defer your start term:

Step 4: Online+ students, please contact mari.kate.mclaughlin@ttu.edu.

Step 5: Grad+ students please contact online.gradprograms@ttu.edu

What is Texas Tech Online+ (TTU Online+)?

TTU Online+ is a fully online, student-centered learning model at Texas Tech University designed with structured support, 8-week courses, and dedicated staff to help students succeed from start to finish.
